messages:
caroline: quick follow-up on the signer-escrow + operator rehydrate playbook RFC — opened this thread to gather concrete operator steps and any missing safety nets. TL;DR: we want a minimal offline recovery flow for when a site loses control-plane access but still has an admin box and physical media. idea: escrowed signed bundles + a verified rehydrate tool that applies deltas and can roll back if hashes mismatch.

juan: +1. can we avoid adding a new binary for operators? maybe use the existing `rh-upgrade` agent but with an `--rehydrate` flag. keeps surface area small.

samir: important: escrowed signer keys must not be single-point-of-failure. propose split-keystore: primary key in KMS, secondary offline signing key stored on HSM/USB. recovery flow uses a quorum: control-plane signature OR operator-escrow signature.

lina: +1 to quorum. also need clear UX: operator should not have to decide which signature to trust at apply time. flow should be deterministic: if CP reachable -> prefer CP signature. else -> require operator PIN + 2-person auth to use escrow key.

ops-bot: deploy-notify: new RFC-impl branch created: github.com/redwood-inference/onprem-rehydrate/tree/rfc-escrow. CI: redwood-build/rehydrate-tool.

caroline: proposal for runbook steps (draft):
1) operator verifies media integrity: `sha256sum bundle.tar.gz` -> compare to printed manifest
2) run: `rh-upgrade --rehydrate --bundle bundle.tar.gz`
3) tool validates signatures: primary, fallback-escrow, and signature metadata.
4) if validation passes -> tool stages files, snapshots current /opt/redwood, applies files atomically, updates manifest link.
5) post-apply sanity checks: service healthchecks, token-store connectivity (local), and simple sample inference run.
6) if failure -> tool auto-rolls back to snapshot and emits artifact for offline analysis.

patrick: a few nitpicks:
- step1: manifest needs to be human-readable and include signature counters and signer-ids.
- step3: what about signature rotation? operator-escrow key should have an expiry and transparent rotation mechanism.

samir: on rotation: escrow keys should be ROLLING rather than ephemeral. propose a rotation bundle that contains new escrow pubkeys signed by CP and an operator confirmation token. rotation should be applied during normal upgrades, not during emergency rehydrate.

juan: question: how do we handle partial delta application? if the rehydrate bundle is "delta-from-previous" but the node is several versions behind, rehydrate tool must be able to ingest a chain of deltas or fail-fast with clear error. prefer: accept both full bundle and chained deltas.

caroline: yes, tool should accept `bundle.tar.gz` which can be either a full image or a signed sequence of deltas. behaviour: if chain needed -> tool applies deltas sequentially with verification at each step.

lina: operator auth UX: recommend 2 prompts: 1) operator name + reason (freeform), 2) hardware-PIN or smartcard confirmation. log both to local audit in `/var/log/rh-rehydrate.log` (encrypted at rest).

patrick: for encryption at rest, don't reinvent: integrate with OS LUKS or rely on container storage encryption. also capture in runbook how to redact logs before sharing.

ops-bot: note: IANA: tagging follow-up item: "rehydrate-runbook-checklist" -> created page in confluence: /onprem/runbooks/rehydrate-playbook-draft (link internal).

samir: corner case: what if operator applies escrow-signed bundle but CP later shows up and flags a different manifest? We need canonical conflict resolution. proposal: roll-forward rule: CP manifest supersedes escrowed manifest if CP timestamp > escrow manifest timestamp AND CP manifest signature chain verifies to a known CP key. we should also record that node performed offline rehydrate (for auditing).

caroline: agree. add to runbook: after rehydrate, operator should attempt to re-establish control-plane connection and run `rh-check-in` which will compare local manifest -> CP manifest and surface diffs. If mismatch, CP can push a reconciled delta or instruct operator to trigger a safe roll.

juan: small implementation detail: staging snapshot should be copy-on-write where possible to reduce downtime for large model files. use `rsync --link-dest` pattern to avoid full copies. mention in runbook.

lina: can we also include a minimal offline healthcheck binary that runs inside airgapped environment to validate critical signals (model loads, kv-store read/writes)? keep it under 50KB so it's easy to transport.

patrick: +1 but test harness first. add acceptance test that simulates: 1) control-plane down, 2) operator rehydrate via USB, 3) reconciliation when CP returns. we should automate in CI using `qemu` for a lightweight node image.

caroline: action items from thread:
- samir: draft escrow key rotation proposal (deadline: 3 business days)
- juan: prototype `--rehydrate` flag on rh-upgrade and rsync snapshot approach (deadline: 1 week)
- lina: write operator UX section and minimal offline healthcheck binary spec (deadline: 4 business days)
- patrick: add CI acceptance test skeleton for rehydrate flow (deadline: 2 weeks)
- caroline: consolidate runbook and push to confluence, link the RFC branch (today)

ops-bot: reminder: meeting scheduled — "escrow & rehydrate sync" Tue 10:00 PT.

juan: one more thought: we should provide an "audit pack" command that bundles logs, manifests, and signatures into an encrypted artifact the operator can hand to security. `rh-rehydrate --collect-audit > audit-pack.tar.gz`

samir: sounds good. ensure audit-pack redacts secrets but includes signature metadata and signer fingerprints.

lina: ok I'm starting the UX doc now, will ping when ready for review. :+1:

caroline: thanks all — this thread captured the main follow-ups. We'll iterate on the confluence doc and aim for a small RFC amendment with concrete CLI surface/steps.
